mission: PBUF FND-003 Three-Dimensional Microscopic State Justification

three_dimensional_state.geometric_state: q(x) in T_x Sigma (or T_x^* Sigma), with dim(Sigma)=3
three_dimensional_state.components: q^a=e^a(q), a=1,2,3, in a local orthonormal frame
three_dimensional_state.rotation_law: q'^a=R^a_b q^b for R in SO(3)
three_dimensional_state.status: minimal conditional realization, not a consequence of dimensionality alone

continuum_mappings: Requires an additional transforming vector e; a fixed background e breaks isotropy
Rotation scalar without an internal direction
Introduces a derivative and length L; does not equal the CORE-001 map
Nonlinear, nonnegative, and changes the weak-field/source expansion

remaining_postulates.text: The microscopic state carries the defining spatial-vector (or covector) representation of SO(3), rather than a scalar, tensor, spinorial, or unrelated internal representation.
remaining_postulates.needed_for: identifying three components with three spatial directions

remaining_postulates.text: The rotation action is linear and faithful and all three directional responses are independent; no additional microscopic sectors are required.
A covariant scalarization mechanism is selected: a matter-provided vector e, a longitudinal derivative, or a nonlinear invariant.
remaining_postulates.needed_for: mapping q to the scalar continuum field u

remaining_postulates.text: The stable, local, isotropic long-wave expansion and decoupling assumptions of CORE-001/FND-002 hold.
If g_dev=1/137 is to be derived rather than postulated, a microscopic principle must fix its value and specify any applicable scale behavior.
remaining_postulates.needed_for: turning 1/137 from a direct PBUF premise into a prediction

recommendation: FND-004 covariant representation, scalarization, mode-decoupling, and coupling-identifiability development
